name: The Ash of Kleverlaan
verified_sources: https://www.ivn.nl/afdeling/zuid-kennemerland/natuuractiviteiten/monumentale-bomen-op-de-begraafplaats/ (confirms the cemetery as a designated stop for monumental-tree walks; general corroboration of setting, not tree-specific)
access: Free, public cemetery (Algemene Begraafplaats Kleverlaan), open during normal daytime hours
transport: Tram or bus to Kleverpark, then a short walk, roughly 15-20 minutes from central Haarlem (same stop as the already-published Kleverlaan Yew, haa_003)
verify_notes: Register nr 1696652, planted band 1870-1880, visitable=yes, visible=yes, n_trees=1. Register's own place text: 'Aan de zuidkant in het oude gedeelte van het begraafpark op een inham van het pad bij een aantal graven' (on the south side, in the old section of the cemetery park, at a bend in the path near several graves). Only the LRMB register found as a source; general cemetery-tree corroboration exists (IVN, haarlemupdates, dodenakkers.nl all describe this cemetery as a designated monumental-tree site with century-old beeches, cypress, cedar, walnut, yew) but none names this specific ash. Sits about 90-150 m from the already-published Kleverlaan Yew (haa_003) and the rest of this cluster, so it joins an existing walkable stop rather than opening a new one.

name: The Zocher Beeches

location.address: Algemene Begraafplaats Kleverlaan, east side near Schoterweg, Haarlem

verified_sources: https://www.dodenakkers.nl/noord-holland/kleverlaan.html and https://www.online-begraafplaatsen.nl/begraafplaats/914/Begraafplaats-Kleverlaan-Haarlem (both independently confirm the graves of father and son Zocher, the cemetery's own landscape designers, lie in this cemetery near Schoterweg, matching the register's stated location for this beech group; general/contextual corroboration of the naming, not a direct tree-specific source)
access: Free, public cemetery, open during normal daytime hours
transport: Tram or bus to Kleverpark, then a short walk, roughly 15-20 minutes from central Haarlem
verify_notes: Register nr 1691633 records THREE beeches together ('Zocherbeuk', n_trees=3) at 'Oostzijde Algemene begraafplaats Kleverlaan, nabij Schoterweg' (east side of the cemetery, near Schoterweg), planted band 1800-1850, visitable=yes, visible=yes. A WebSearch AI summary (not independently confirmed on a fetched page, so treated as a lead only per BRIEF_RESEARCH's search-summary rule) claimed the beeches are named for J.D. Zocher senior and junior, the cemetery's own landscape architects, buried at their foot, with one figure of '170+ years old, 4m circumference' that could NOT be verified on any page this session actually loaded; that specific figure is deliberately excluded from age_estimate and girth_cm. What IS independently confirmed by two directly-fetched sources (dodenakkers.nl, online-begraafplaatsen.nl) is that both Zochers are indeed buried in this cemetery near Schoterweg, which matches the register's own location for this beech group and supports the register's naming, without confirming the burial-at-the-foot detail specifically. Treated as one collectible ensemble (three co-located beeches at one grave site), consistent with this city's existing Oak Pair precedent (haa_011).

name: The Plane of Frederikspark

location.address: Frederikspark, opposite the former ABN bank office, Houtplein, Haarlem

verified_sources: https://www.boomkronen.eu/node/99 (Pius Floris professional tree-care record: stem diameter 175 cm, height 24 m, for the plane tree at Frederikspark)
access: Free, public park, open at any time
transport: About 20-25 minute walk from Haarlem Centraal Station, or a short bus ride to Houtplein
verify_notes: Register nr 1686319, planted band 1860-1870, visitable=yes, visible=yes, n_trees=1, place text 'Tegenover A.B.N.kantoor, Houtplein' (opposite the former ABN bank office, Houtplein). Independently corroborated by boomkronen.eu (Pius Floris, a professional tree-care firm), which records this Frederikspark plane at 175 cm stem diameter (girth_cm derived as pi x 175 = 550 cm) and 24 m height; that page gave no age directly, so age_estimate here is derived from the register's own planted band rather than from the girth figure, to avoid a bridge claim. Two independent sources agree with no conflict, the strongest-evidenced candidate from this session.
